Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill sets up how levies on airlines and airports are collected to pay for a new consumer protection regulator.
The Aviation Consumer Protection Authority would enforce minimum service standards for passengers, while a separate ombudsperson would handle individual complaints.
The levy and collection bills would start at the same time as the main Aviation Consumer Protection Bill and a related transitional bill.
Establishes procedures for collecting and administering cost recovery charges from regulated entities.
Allows regulations to set payment due dates, permit instalments, and provide for late payment penalties and waivers.
Ensures the levies fund the Aviation Consumer Protection Authority's regulatory activities.
Airlines, airports, and other regulated entities in the aviation industry would pay the levies.
